utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Mission Viejo' by name among the cities in its service area. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the City of Mission Viejo's own Eligibility Checklist for Expedited Solar Photovoltaic Permitting explicitly includes a checkbox for applicants to specify their electric utility as either 'SDG&E' or 'SCE', directly confirming Mission Viejo (like neighboring Laguna Niguel and Laguna Hills) is split between SCE and San Diego Gas & Electric territory. This record covers the SCE-served portion of the city only. Confidence reduced from the usual 0.9 to reflect this genuine split-territory complexity.

generation_supplier.notes: Orange County Power Authority (OCPA), the CCA operating in Orange County, currently names Buena Park, Fullerton, Irvine, and Fountain Valley as members — Mission Viejo was not named among current members this session (only identified as a city that theoretically 'may want to join'). Left null rather than asserted either way.

county.notes: Mission Viejo is a well-documented Orange County city; also listed under Orange County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of Mission Viejo Building Division

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — applies only to the SCE-served portion of Mission Viejo; SDG&E-served residents would use SDG&E's own NEM program instead, which was not researched for this city this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its own distribution territory, which includes the SCE-served portion of Mission Viejo/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact — applies to the SCE-served portion of the city only.

value.name: Completed Eligibility Checklist for Expedited Solar Photovoltaic Permitting (job address, contractor/engineer license info, system size, module count, disconnects, conduit length, inverter count)
Structural Criteria documentation, or (if any structural checklist item fails) project-specific drawings and calculations wet-stamped and signed by a California-licensed civil or structural engineer
Roof plan/diagram of module and anchor layout, clear access pathways, and electrical disconnect/roof access point locations

value: Schedule, cancel, and confirm inspections through the Client Self Service online portal
Inspections are conducted the next business day; requests must be submitted before 4:00 PM the day before the desired inspection date
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Services inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited Solar Photovoltaic Permitting (One- and Two-Family Dwellings, under 10kW AC)
other_conditions: Roof-mounted on a one- or two-family dwelling or accessory structure
Panel/module arrays cannot exceed the maximum legal building height
System must be utility-interactive and without battery storage to qualify for the expedited pathway

Electrical: no more than 4 PV strings per MPPT input with source-circuit fusing in the inverter (2 without), no more than 2 inverters for central-string systems, single-phase AC service panel of 120/220 Vac with a bus bar rating of 225A or less, connected to the load side of utility distribution equipment

Structural: detailed roof/rafter/anchor spacing checks (Tables 1 and 2 in the city's own document) — e.g. PV arrays limited to 4 psf max weight, array covering no more than half the total roof area, flush-mounted with a 2-10 inch gap from the roof surface
Fire safety: clear access pathways, fire classification, required markings/labels, and a roof layout diagram
